headline: A 15-year-old in South Korea claims that, with help from Anthropic's Claude AI, he has shown that one solid shape cannot pass through a hole in a copy of itself, but experts say the claim needs rigorous review.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the paper was posted on 5 Oct 2026, before this window, and the claim is unreviewed.
importance_line: Students, teachers and amateur mathematicians who use AI to attempt research are affected first, then mathematicians and journals that must decide how to judge AI-assisted work, but the proof has not been peer reviewed, the author says he cannot verify every detail, and the matching conclusion in another paper is his own report.
summary: Korea JoongAng Daily reports that Jung Gi-hyo, a ninth grader at Gimpohangaram Middle School in Gyeonggi, posted a paper on 5 Oct 2026 claiming, with code written by Claude and about 38 hours of laptop calculation, that the rhombicosidodecahedron, a solid made of triangles, squares and pentagons, cannot pass through a hole in an identical copy of itself, which would disprove a conjecture that every convex solid can. Experts quoted at the Institute for Basic Science and Seoul National University say posting on a repository does not guarantee validity, and Jung says he cannot verify every detail but that another paper reached the same conclusion by a different route.
notes: Older news re-dated: the paper was posted on 5 Oct 2026; the JoongAng report is dated 14 Oct 2026 (it says 'on Tuesday', 13 Oct). Claim is unreviewed. An editor may keep it as the first press report of the claim.
